summary: An interactive educational project for kids from 6 to 12 years old, that lets the child live the role of an astronaut.The app shows a picture of an astronaut's tool, and the child chooses its name and its use from the options, then finds out if his answer is right or wrong.After that, he enters stages of exploring the Sun and planets, solves challenges, collects points, and levels up like a game.The goal: The child learns real facts about space, knows astronauts' tools, and trains to think and solve problems on his own.
details:
AstroKids is an interactive, space-themed educational web game designed for children. Players embark on a 10-level cosmic journey where they guide a rocket along a starry path through different planets. Each level unlocks a space mission featuring visual questions about rockets, astronauts, telescopes, and satellites. When a player answers a question, they receive immediate feedback along with a simple scientific explanation to reinforce their learning before advancing to the next stage. Benefits & Intended Impact:

The project aims to spark curiosity about space exploration and STEM fields among young learners. By transforming complex space concepts—such as how rockets launch, how astronauts breathe and stay protected in space, and how satellites use solar energy—into a fun, step-by-step challenge, AstroKids makes science accessible, engaging, and easy to understand for kids. Tools & Technologies Used:

• HTML5: Used to structure the game interface, level map, and quiz sections.

• CSS3: Used to design the space environment, glowing animations, planets, starry backgrounds, and responsive layout.

• JavaScript (Vanilla JS): Used to build the game logic, rocket movement, level-unlocking system, score/progress tracking, and interactive feedback.

• SVG: Used to draw the curved dashed flight path connecting the 10 space levels.

• Visual Studio Code: Used as the primary code editor for development and testing.

Creativity & Team Considerations:

Our creativity shines through the gamified "Space Mission" map, where a rocket physically moves from planet to planet as children progress. Our team carefully considered the target age group (children) by ensuring:

• Simplicity & Clarity: Short, easy-to-read questions with clear multiple-choice options.

• Visual Engagement: High-contrast space colors, emojis, and real space imagery to keep children focused.

• Constructive Learning: Instead of just marking an answer wrong, the game explains why the correct answer works in real space missions.
